words.definitionEn: a very large quantity of something
words.exampleDailyEn: Our garden produces an abundance of tomatoes every summer.
words.exampleIeltsEn: An abundance of natural resources does not necessarily guarantee sustainable economic growth or improved living standards.

words.definitionEn: The gradual gathering of something, or the amount gathered.
words.exampleDailyEn: An accumulation of dust covered the old wooden shelves.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The accumulation of plastic waste in oceans threatens marine wildlife and creates lasting challenges for coastal communities.

words.definitionEn: the process of obtaining something or developing knowledge and skills
words.exampleDailyEn: Daily conversations helped with her acquisition of new vocabulary.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Early exposure to varied speech can support language acquisition and strengthen children's ability to communicate effectively.

words.definitionEn: To follow a rule, belief, or agreement closely.
words.exampleDailyEn: Everyone must adhere to the rules in this pool.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Researchers must adhere to strict ethical standards when collecting personal information from participants in health studies.

words.definitionEn: to manage an organization or put a system into operation
words.exampleDailyEn: The nurse administered the medicine before I went home.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Local authorities administer housing programmes designed to provide affordable accommodation for families on low incomes.

words.definitionEn: To publicly support a policy, idea, or course of action.
words.exampleDailyEn: Our neighbours advocate planting more trees along the street.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Many health professionals advocate regular physical activity as an affordable way to prevent chronic disease.

words.definitionEn: To assign resources to particular people, activities, or purposes.
words.exampleDailyEn: We allocated one cupboard to all our baking equipment.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Local authorities should allocate more funding to public transport in areas with limited access to essential services.

words.definitionEn: To change a document, rule, or plan to improve it.
words.exampleDailyEn: Please amend the booking to include one extra guest.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Parliament may amend existing legislation to ensure that remote workers receive the same protections as office employees.

words.definitionEn: A change made to a law, document, or proposal.
words.exampleDailyEn: We agreed on one small amendment to the contract.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The proposed amendment would require employers to provide safer working conditions for temporary staff.

words.definitionEn: A comparison used to explain something through a similar example
words.exampleDailyEn: Her analogy compared our busy kitchen to a train station.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Teachers often draw an analogy between electrical circuits and flowing water to explain unfamiliar scientific concepts.

words.definitionEn: a large collection of different things
words.exampleDailyEn: The bakery displayed a colourful array of cakes.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Modern universities offer a wide array of courses to meet the demands of a changing labour market.

words.definitionEn: able to express ideas clearly and effectively
words.exampleDailyEn: Our articulate neighbour explained the problem clearly at dinner.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Schools should help students articulate their opinions clearly while encouraging them to consider alternative perspectives.

words.definitionEn: A strong hope or ambition to achieve something.
words.exampleDailyEn: Her greatest aspiration is to open a small bakery.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Access to affordable higher education can help young people fulfil their aspirations, regardless of their family income.

words.definitionEn: To strongly want to achieve something important.
words.exampleDailyEn: My younger sister aspires to become a wildlife photographer.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Many young people aspire to careers that offer both financial security and opportunities to contribute to society.
collocations: aspire to a career in medicine

words.definitionEn: the deliberate murder of an important person, often for political reasons
words.exampleDailyEn: The museum guide explained how the assassination changed history.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The assassination of a political leader can trigger widespread instability and undermine public confidence in government.

words.definitionEn: a violent physical attack on someone
words.exampleDailyEn: A witness reported the assault to a nearby police officer.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Better street lighting may reduce the risk of assault and help residents feel safer after dark.

words.definitionEn: To state firmly that something is true.
words.exampleDailyEn: He asserted that he had already paid for lunch.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Some educators assert that regular feedback improves student motivation more effectively than frequent formal examinations.

words.definitionEn: a confident statement that something is true
words.exampleDailyEn: Her assertion that the shop was closed proved wrong.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The assertion that economic growth always improves wellbeing requires careful examination of social and environmental evidence.

words.definitionEn: A promise intended to remove doubt or worry.
words.exampleDailyEn: She gave me her assurance that dinner was ready.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Residents sought an assurance from the council that the new development would not reduce access to public parks.

words.definitionEn: Protection a country gives people escaping danger in another country.
words.exampleDailyEn: Her family sought asylum after fleeing their home country.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments should assess asylum applications fairly while ensuring that vulnerable applicants have access to legal advice.

words.definitionEn: To reach a goal or level, usually through effort.
words.exampleDailyEn: After months of practice, she attained her target swimming speed.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Students from disadvantaged backgrounds may need additional support to attain the qualifications required for university entry.

words.definitionEn: To give official permission for someone to do something.
words.exampleDailyEn: Only the manager can authorize a refund this large.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Local authorities may authorize new housing developments only after assessing their likely effects on traffic and public services.

words.definitionEn: The freedom or right to make decisions independently.
words.exampleDailyEn: My new manager gives me more autonomy at work.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Giving schools greater autonomy may help teachers adapt their lessons to the specific needs of local communities.

words.definitionEn: A process of voting, usually in secret.
words.exampleDailyEn: Our club chose its new chair by secret ballot.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A secret ballot allows citizens to express their political preferences without fear of pressure from others.

words.definitionEn: an administrative system run by officials following established rules
words.exampleDailyEn: My aunt works within the city's large bureaucracy.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Reducing unnecessary bureaucracy could help small businesses obtain permits more quickly without weakening essential safety standards.

words.definitionEn: an economic system based on private ownership and profit
words.exampleDailyEn: We discussed capitalism over coffee after our economics class.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Critics of capitalism argue that governments should regulate markets to limit inequality and protect vulnerable workers.

words.definitionEn: to stop happening or doing something
words.exampleDailyEn: The bells finally ceased ringing just before midnight.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Factories should cease discharging untreated wastewater into rivers to protect aquatic ecosystems and safeguard public health.

words.definitionEn: A room used for a particular, often official, purpose.
words.exampleDailyEn: We waited outside the chamber while the council met.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The upper chamber of parliament reviews proposed laws before they can receive final approval.

words.definitionEn: To be a typical or distinguishing feature of something.
words.exampleDailyEn: Bright colours and bold patterns characterize her handmade bags.
words.exampleIeltsEn: High housing costs and limited public space characterize many large cities, affecting residents' quality of life.

words.definitionEn: The quality of being clear and easy to understand.
words.exampleDailyEn: I appreciate the clarity of your instructions for this game.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Greater clarity in public health advice can help people make informed decisions about their daily habits.

words.definitionEn: a group of similar things positioned or occurring close together
words.exampleDailyEn: A cluster of purple flowers grew beside the gate.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Technology companies often cluster near universities, where they can recruit skilled graduates and collaborate with researchers.

words.definitionEn: to happen at the same time
words.exampleDailyEn: My days off rarely coincide with my sister's.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Government investment should coincide with local priorities to ensure that public funds address genuine community needs.

words.definitionEn: work with others to create or achieve something
words.exampleDailyEn: We collaborate on recipes for our weekend cooking club.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Universities should collaborate with local businesses to develop practical solutions to regional environmental problems.

words.definitionEn: to begin something or start happening
words.exampleDailyEn: The evening concert will commence after a short welcome.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Construction of the new railway will commence once the environmental assessment has been completed.

words.definitionEn: an official responsible for a public service or commission
words.exampleDailyEn: The commissioner visited our neighbourhood to discuss road safety.
words.exampleIeltsEn: An independent commissioner should investigate public complaints and ensure that government agencies treat citizens fairly.

words.definitionEn: to force someone to do something
words.exampleDailyEn: Heavy rain compelled us to cancel our picnic.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Stricter environmental laws could compel manufacturers to reduce waste and adopt cleaner production methods.

words.definitionEn: Collect information from different sources and arrange it together.
words.exampleDailyEn: We compiled a playlist for our long train journey.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Researchers compiled data from several hospitals to examine the relationship between air pollution and childhood asthma.

words.definitionEn: the act of following a rule, law, or request
words.exampleDailyEn: The inspector checked our kitchen for compliance with hygiene rules.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Regular inspections can improve compliance with environmental regulations and reduce pollution from industrial facilities.

words.definitionEn: to have particular people or things as parts
words.exampleDailyEn: The gift set comprises soap, lotion, and a towel.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The proposed transport network will comprise bus routes and cycle lanes connecting residential areas with employment centres.

words.definitionEn: To calculate an amount or result, often using a computer.
words.exampleDailyEn: This app computes the cost of our weekly shopping.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Researchers compute average temperatures from satellite data to assess long-term changes in the global climate.

words.definitionEn: To admit something is true, often unwillingly
words.exampleDailyEn: He finally conceded that my route was much quicker.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Although critics concede that tourism creates jobs, they argue that its environmental costs are often overlooked.

words.definitionEn: to form an idea or imagine something
words.exampleDailyEn: She conceived the idea while walking through the park.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Urban planners must conceive new ways of accommodating population growth without sacrificing green spaces or affordable housing.

words.definitionEn: an idea or understanding of what something is like
words.exampleDailyEn: His conception of a perfect holiday involves no phones.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Access to green spaces can broaden children's conception of nature beyond what they learn in classrooms.

words.definitionEn: Something accepted or given up to help reach an agreement
words.exampleDailyEn: We made a concession and agreed to leave earlier.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Offering concessions to students and older people can make public transport more affordable for these groups.

words.definitionEn: To express strong disapproval of someone or something.
words.exampleDailyEn: Our neighbours condemned the dumping of rubbish beside the river.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Environmental organisations condemn illegal logging because it destroys wildlife habitats and threatens the livelihoods of local communities.

words.definitionEn: Discuss something with others before making a decision.
words.exampleDailyEn: The coaches conferred quietly before choosing the final team.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Universities often confer honorary degrees on individuals who have made outstanding contributions to science or public service.

words.definitionEn: To keep something within particular limits
words.exampleDailyEn: Please confine your muddy boots to the porch.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Researchers should not confine their investigation to wealthy neighbourhoods when studying access to public transport.

words.definitionEn: General agreement among members of a group.
words.exampleDailyEn: We finally reached a consensus on where to eat.
words.exampleIeltsEn: There is a broad consensus among researchers that early childhood education can improve children's future learning outcomes.

words.definitionEn: To make an achievement, position, or skill stronger.
words.exampleDailyEn: I review my notes each evening to consolidate my learning.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Regular practical exercises help students consolidate their knowledge and apply theoretical concepts to unfamiliar situations.

words.definitionEn: A secret plan by several people to do something wrong.
words.exampleDailyEn: Police uncovered a conspiracy to steal valuable paintings.
words.exampleIeltsEn: False conspiracy theories can spread rapidly online, weakening public trust in scientific institutions.

words.definitionEn: To be the parts that form a whole
words.exampleDailyEn: Vegetables constitute most of the food in our fridge.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Rising housing costs constitute a major barrier to financial independence for young adults in large cities.

words.definitionEn: Something that limits what you can do.
words.exampleDailyEn: Our main constraint is the size of the kitchen.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Financial constraints prevent many local authorities from investing adequately in reliable public transport.

words.definitionEn: to think carefully about something for a long time
words.exampleDailyEn: She sat beside the lake, contemplating her next move.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Before expanding public transport, planners should contemplate how proposed routes will affect existing communities.

words.definitionEn: A strong feeling that someone or something deserves no respect
words.exampleDailyEn: He showed contempt for my suggestion by laughing.
words.exampleIeltsEn: When officials treat public concerns with contempt, trust in democratic institutions can decline significantly.

words.definitionEn: To argue that something is true.
words.exampleDailyEn: I contend that our kitchen needs a bigger table.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Some researchers contend that affordable public transport is more effective than road expansion in reducing urban congestion.

words.definitionEn: A difference between statements or facts that cannot both be true
words.exampleDailyEn: I noticed a contradiction between his two explanations.
words.exampleIeltsEn: There is a clear contradiction between promoting sustainable transport and reducing investment in local bus services.

words.definitionEn: Someone found guilty of a crime, especially someone in prison.
words.exampleDailyEn: The former convict now works at a local bakery.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Education programmes can help a convict develop practical skills and prepare for employment after release from prison.

words.definitionEn: Written communication between people, or the messages they exchange.
words.exampleDailyEn: She keeps her correspondence with her cousin in a drawer.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Historical correspondence can reveal how ordinary families experienced social changes that official records describe only briefly.

words.definitionEn: Someone or something with a similar role in another setting.
words.exampleDailyEn: Our team leader met her counterpart from another branch.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Urban schools often have better access to specialist teachers than their rural counterparts, reinforcing educational inequality.

words.definitionEn: A standard used to judge something or make a decision.
words.exampleDailyEn: Price was my main criterion when choosing a bicycle.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Environmental impact should be a key criterion when governments assess proposals for new transport infrastructure.

words.definitionEn: To prepare land for crops or grow plants
words.exampleDailyEn: My grandparents cultivate vegetables in a small garden behind their house.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Schools should cultivate curiosity by encouraging students to ask questions and explore different solutions to practical problems.

words.definitionEn: Intended to hurt someone through harsh criticism or unkind remarks.
words.exampleDailyEn: His cutting remark about her cooking spoiled the meal.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Cutting comments from teachers can discourage students from asking questions and participating actively in class.

words.definitionEn: To judge or consider someone or something in a particular way.
words.exampleDailyEn: The inspector deemed our old boiler unsafe to use.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public transport should be deemed an essential service rather than merely a source of profit.

words.definitionEn: A lack of enough of something necessary.
words.exampleDailyEn: A blood test revealed that I had an iron deficiency.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Nutritional deficiency among children can affect physical growth and reduce their ability to concentrate at school.

words.definitionEn: the amount by which spending exceeds income
words.exampleDailyEn: Our club faces a deficit after buying new equipment.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments may reduce a budget deficit by raising taxes, but this can slow economic growth.

words.definitionEn: to show or describe something in art, images, or words
words.exampleDailyEn: This painting depicts children playing beside a quiet lake.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Films often depict urban life as exciting, overlooking the isolation that many residents experience in large cities.

words.definitionEn: To officially choose someone or something for a particular purpose.
words.exampleDailyEn: We designated one cupboard for all our cleaning supplies.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Local authorities should designate more urban land as protected green space to improve residents' quality of life.

words.definitionEn: To cause very severe damage to a place or thing
words.exampleDailyEn: The storm devastated the village, leaving many homes damaged.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Prolonged droughts can devastate agricultural communities by destroying crops and reducing the income available to farming households.

words.definitionEn: To recognize or explain the differences between things
words.exampleDailyEn: Can you differentiate these two birds by their songs?
words.exampleIeltsEn: Schools should teach students to differentiate between reliable evidence and unsupported claims in online media.

words.definitionEn: to become smaller or weaker, or make something so
words.exampleDailyEn: The pain in my ankle gradually diminished overnight.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Investment in reliable public transport can diminish dependence on private cars and improve air quality in crowded cities.

words.definitionEn: to make previously private or unknown information available
words.exampleDailyEn: The hotel would not disclose any details about its guests.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Companies should disclose how they collect personal data so that consumers can make informed decisions.

words.definitionEn: Serious spoken or written discussion of a particular subject.
words.exampleDailyEn: Her lecture encouraged thoughtful discourse about local history.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public discourse on climate change increasingly focuses on practical solutions rather than distant predictions.

words.definitionEn: care in speaking or acting to avoid embarrassment or harm
words.exampleDailyEn: Please use discretion when discussing her private life.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Teachers need some discretion to adapt classroom activities to the needs of individual learners.

words.definitionEn: Force people to leave their homes or usual surroundings.
words.exampleDailyEn: The flood displaced several families living near the river.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Although automation may displace some workers, investment in retraining can help them find alternative employment.

words.definitionEn: to present information in a misleading or inaccurate way
words.exampleDailyEn: That edited clip distorts what I actually said.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Selective reporting can distort public understanding of environmental issues and weaken support for necessary reforms.

words.definitionEn: A belief or set of principles taught by a group.
words.exampleDailyEn: The guide explained the doctrine behind the temple's daily rituals.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Economic doctrine should be evaluated against practical evidence rather than accepted simply because it has influential supporters.

words.definitionEn: a particular area of knowledge, activity, or responsibility
words.exampleDailyEn: Electrical repairs are my brother's domain, not mine.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Environmental protection should not be regarded as the exclusive domain of scientists, since public participation is essential.

words.definitionEn: To replace a film's original speech with another language.
words.exampleDailyEn: They dubbed the cartoon into Spanish for younger viewers.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Journalists have dubbed the new railway a lifeline for rural communities previously isolated from major employment centres.

words.definitionEn: To move something to a higher physical position
words.exampleDailyEn: The nurse used a pillow to elevate my ankle.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Access to advanced training can elevate professional standards and improve the quality of public services.

words.definitionEn: To begin a project, activity, or course of action
words.exampleDailyEn: We are ready to embark on our kitchen renovation.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Before students embark on professional training, they should consider both their interests and future employment opportunities.

words.definitionEn: to fix something firmly inside a surrounding material
words.exampleDailyEn: The artist embedded small shells in the wet clay.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Schools should embed environmental awareness in everyday lessons rather than discuss sustainability only on special occasions.

words.definitionEn: To clearly represent an idea, quality, or feeling.
words.exampleDailyEn: These handmade bowls embody my grandmother's patience and care.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public buildings should embody the values of inclusion by providing accessible spaces for people with different needs.

words.definitionEn: Give someone confidence or control over their own life.
words.exampleDailyEn: Learning to cook empowered him to live independently.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Access to reliable information can empower citizens to make informed decisions about their health.

words.definitionEn: To make a proposal officially become law.
words.exampleDailyEn: The children enacted a scene from their favourite story.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments should enact legislation that protects vulnerable workers without placing excessive financial burdens on small businesses.

words.definitionEn: A serious effort to achieve something.
words.exampleDailyEn: Growing vegetables together became our family's latest endeavour.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments should endeavour to make reliable public transport accessible to people in remote communities.

words.definitionEn: Make sure that people obey a law or rule.
words.exampleDailyEn: The pool staff enforce strict rules about running indoors.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments must enforce environmental regulations consistently if they want industries to reduce pollution and protect public health.

words.definitionEn: To improve something by adding value, interest, or experience.
words.exampleDailyEn: These weekend painting classes really enrich my daily life.
words.exampleIeltsEn: International exchange programmes can enrich students' education by exposing them to different perspectives and teaching methods.

words.definitionEn: To happen after something, often as its result.
words.exampleDailyEn: A lively discussion ensued after dinner at our house.
words.exampleIeltsEn: If public services fail to meet growing demand, widespread dissatisfaction may ensue among local residents.

words.definitionEn: something that exists independently, especially an organization
words.exampleDailyEn: Our small bakery now operates as a separate entity.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Each university should remain an independent entity while cooperating with other institutions on important research projects.

words.definitionEn: to build something or put it in an upright position
words.exampleDailyEn: We erected our tent beside the lake before sunset.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Local authorities plan to erect temporary shelters for families whose homes were damaged by severe flooding.

words.definitionEn: the most important quality that makes something what it is
words.exampleDailyEn: For me, the essence of friendship is being there.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The essence of sustainable development is meeting present needs without limiting opportunities for future generations.

words.definitionEn: the process of starting an organisation or system
words.exampleDailyEn: The establishment of our local club brought neighbours together.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The establishment of protected marine areas can help restore fish populations and support coastal communities.

words.definitionEn: to bring a feeling, memory or image into someone's mind
words.exampleDailyEn: The smell of fresh bread evokes memories of home.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Traditional music can evoke a strong sense of belonging among people living far from their homeland.

words.definitionEn: the act of carrying out a plan, order, or task
words.exampleDailyEn: The picnic plan was simple, but its execution proved tricky.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Successful execution of environmental policies requires adequate funding, clear responsibilities, and consistent monitoring by public authorities.

words.definitionEn: To apply force, influence, or authority.
words.exampleDailyEn: You must exert steady pressure to open this lid.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Parents can exert considerable influence on children's eating habits by preparing balanced meals at home.

words.definitionEn: Forced absence from one's own country, often for political reasons
words.exampleDailyEn: After years in exile, she finally returned home.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Many writers living in exile use literature to preserve cultural traditions and describe their experiences of displacement.

words.definitionEn: money spent on something
words.exampleDailyEn: We track our monthly expenditure in a small notebook.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Higher public expenditure on preventive healthcare could reduce the long-term cost of treating chronic diseases.

words.definitionEn: Unfair treatment of people to gain benefits from their work
words.exampleDailyEn: The workers demanded fair wages and protection from exploitation.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The uncontrolled exploitation of natural resources can damage ecosystems and undermine the livelihoods of communities that depend on them.

words.definitionEn: make an action or process easier
words.exampleDailyEn: These sliding doors facilitate access for people using wheelchairs.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Digital platforms can facilitate collaboration between students in different countries, allowing them to exchange ideas more easily.

words.definitionEn: A subgroup whose views conflict with others in a larger group.
words.exampleDailyEn: One faction of our club wants a new leader.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A powerful faction within the ruling party opposed the proposed reforms to the national education system.

words.definitionEn: An achievement requiring great skill, strength, or courage.
words.exampleDailyEn: Carrying that huge sofa upstairs was quite a feat.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Building a railway across mountainous terrain remains an impressive feat of engineering, even with modern technology.

words.definitionEn: A weapon that fires bullets using an explosive charge.
words.exampleDailyEn: The antique firearm was displayed behind thick museum glass.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Strict firearm storage regulations can help prevent accidents and improve safety in homes and communities.

words.definitionEn: To grow strongly or develop successfully.
words.exampleDailyEn: These herbs flourish on our warm, sunny kitchen windowsill.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Small businesses are more likely to flourish when local governments provide affordable premises and reliable public transport.

words.definitionEn: to encourage something to develop or grow
words.exampleDailyEn: Shared meals foster closer friendships among our neighbours.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Schools can foster creativity by allowing students to explore problems without prescribing a single solution.

words.definitionEn: permission to trade under another company's name, or that business
words.exampleDailyEn: My aunt bought a franchise and opened a bakery.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Operating a franchise allows entrepreneurs to use an established business model, but often limits their independence.

words.definitionEn: Acts intended to destroy a national, ethnic, racial, or religious group.
words.exampleDailyEn: We visited a memorial to the victims of genocide.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Education about past acts of genocide can help societies recognise prejudice and strengthen their commitment to human rights.

words.definitionEn: small balls of ice that fall from clouds
words.exampleDailyEn: Hail rattled against the windows during the storm.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Scientists hailed the new irrigation system as a breakthrough that could help farmers conserve water during droughts.

words.definitionEn: to keep returning to someone's mind and causing distress
words.exampleDailyEn: That embarrassing mistake still haunts me before every presentation.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The consequences of poor urban planning can haunt communities long after the original decisions are made.

words.definitionEn: to become stronger or make a feeling or effect stronger
words.exampleDailyEn: The sudden silence only heightened my curiosity about the surprise.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Repeated droughts may heighten public concern about water shortages and encourage governments to invest in conservation.

words.definitionEn: A system arranging people or things by rank or importance
words.exampleDailyEn: There is a clear hierarchy among the restaurant staff.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A rigid workplace hierarchy may discourage junior employees from sharing ideas that could improve organisational performance.

words.definitionEn: A proposed explanation that can be tested through research
words.exampleDailyEn: Our experiment tested the hypothesis that plants prefer sunlight.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Researchers tested the hypothesis that regular physical activity improves concentration among children in primary education.

words.definitionEn: a system of beliefs shaping political or social views
words.exampleDailyEn: Their political ideology shapes how they discuss everyday problems.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Educational policies often reflect the ideology of those in power rather than the needs of learners.

words.definitionEn: to experience costs or something unpleasant because of your actions
words.exampleDailyEn: Late returns may incur an extra charge at this library.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Businesses may incur substantial costs when replacing outdated equipment, but modern technology can improve productivity over time.

words.definitionEn: to reach a conclusion using evidence rather than direct statements
words.exampleDailyEn: From her muddy shoes, I inferred she had been gardening.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Researchers cannot infer that smaller classes improve learning without examining other factors affecting student performance.

words.definitionEn: to cause someone or something to suffer harm
words.exampleDailyEn: The storm inflicted serious damage on our garden fence.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Unregulated industrial activity can inflict lasting damage on ecosystems and threaten the livelihoods of nearby communities.

words.definitionEn: To slow down or prevent a process or activity.
words.exampleDailyEn: Cold weather can inhibit the growth of these plants.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Fear of making mistakes can inhibit students from participating actively in classroom discussions and collaborative tasks.

words.definitionEn: To cause a process or activity to begin.
words.exampleDailyEn: Someone needs to initiate a conversation about the noise.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Local authorities should initiate programmes that encourage residents to recycle household waste more effectively.

words.definitionEn: A person who is kept in a prison.
words.exampleDailyEn: Each inmate can borrow books from the prison library.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Providing inmates with vocational training may improve their employment prospects and reduce the risk of reoffending.

words.definitionEn: Someone within a group who has access to private information.
words.exampleDailyEn: An insider told us the restaurant would reopen next week.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Industry insiders suggest that smaller firms may struggle to meet the costs of stricter environmental regulations.

words.definitionEn: the quality of being honest and following strong moral principles
words.exampleDailyEn: She showed integrity by returning the money she found.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Independent inspections help maintain the structural integrity of bridges and protect the public from preventable accidents.

words.definitionEn: become stronger or more extreme, or make something so
words.exampleDailyEn: The rain intensified as we hurried towards the station.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Rising temperatures may intensify water shortages in regions that already experience long periods of drought.

words.definitionEn: What someone plans or means to do.
words.exampleDailyEn: My intent was to help, not to interrupt you.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Many governments are intent on reducing traffic congestion through investment in reliable public transport.

words.definitionEn: to become involved in a situation to influence what happens
words.exampleDailyEn: The coach intervened before the argument became more heated.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments may need to intervene when market competition fails to provide affordable essential services.

words.definitionEn: A situation that is strikingly opposite to what is expected.
words.exampleDailyEn: The irony is that our swimming lesson was cancelled by rain.

words.definitionEn: A good reason explaining why something is acceptable or necessary.
words.exampleDailyEn: There is no justification for leaving this mess behind.

words.definitionEn: Accepting different opinions and supporting people's freedom to choose.
words.exampleDailyEn: My parents are liberal about what clothes I wear.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A liberal society should protect individual freedoms while encouraging citizens to respect the rights of others.

words.definitionEn: To stay somewhere longer than expected or necessary.
words.exampleDailyEn: We lingered outside the cinema, chatting about the film.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The effects of prolonged unemployment can linger even after individuals return to stable work.

words.definitionEn: Appear as a large, often threatening or unclear shape.
words.exampleDailyEn: A huge ship loomed out of the morning fog.
words.exampleIeltsEn: As water shortages loom, governments must invest in efficient irrigation and encourage households to reduce unnecessary consumption.

words.definitionEn: The size, extent, or importance of something.
words.exampleDailyEn: We only realised the magnitude of the damage at sunrise.

words.definitionEn: something worn or added to make something more attractive
words.exampleDailyEn: A silver brooch was her dress's only adornment.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Traditional jewellery often serves as personal adornment while also expressing cultural identity and social belonging.

words.definitionEn: Giving benefits or improving the chances of success
words.exampleDailyEn: Booking early was advantageous because we got cheaper tickets.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Flexible working arrangements can be advantageous to employers by improving staff satisfaction and reducing employee turnover.

words.definitionEn: The arrival of an important new invention, event, or period
words.exampleDailyEn: The advent of smartphones changed how we take photos.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The advent of affordable renewable energy has encouraged governments to reconsider their dependence on fossil fuels.

words.definitionEn: functioning as an adverb or relating to adverbs
words.exampleDailyEn: Our teacher explained adverbial phrases using simple everyday examples.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Understanding adverbial clauses helps language learners express relationships between events more precisely in academic writing.

words.definitionEn: Harmful or making success and progress more difficult.
words.exampleDailyEn: Our ferry was cancelled because of adverse weather conditions.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Prolonged exposure to traffic noise can have adverse effects on residents' sleep and mental health.

words.definitionEn: A difficult or unfortunate situation that causes hardship.
words.exampleDailyEn: Her friends stood beside her throughout years of adversity.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Strong community networks can help families cope with adversity during periods of economic uncertainty.

words.definitionEn: relating to aircraft or aviation
words.exampleDailyEn: We saw an old aero engine at the museum.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Improvements in aero engine design can reduce fuel consumption and emissions from commercial aircraft.

words.definitionEn: The study of air movement and its effects on objects.
words.exampleDailyEn: We explored aerodynamics by testing paper planes in the garden.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Advances in aerodynamics allow aircraft manufacturers to reduce fuel consumption without significantly compromising passenger capacity or flight speed.

words.definitionEn: A pressurised container that releases liquid as a fine spray.
words.exampleDailyEn: She used an aerosol to spray the dusty leaves.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Atmospheric aerosols can influence the climate by scattering sunlight and altering the formation of clouds.

words.definitionEn: Relating to beauty or the appreciation of beautiful things.
words.exampleDailyEn: The wooden shelves give this room greater aesthetic appeal.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Urban planners should consider both the practical function and aesthetic quality of public spaces.

words.definitionEn: To officially connect a person or group with an organisation.
words.exampleDailyEn: Our local cycling club is affiliated with a national organisation.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Small research institutes often affiliate with universities to gain access to specialist equipment and academic expertise.

words.definitionEn: To state firmly that something is true or supported.
words.exampleDailyEn: Both parents affirmed their support for her career choice.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Schools should affirm the value of cultural diversity by ensuring that teaching materials reflect different backgrounds and experiences.

words.definitionEn: Cause someone or something serious suffering or difficulty
words.exampleDailyEn: Seasonal allergies afflict my brother whenever the flowers bloom.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Water shortages continue to afflict rural communities, limiting agricultural production and increasing the burden on local families.

words.definitionEn: the process of combining separate items into a larger whole
words.exampleDailyEn: Automatic aggregation brings all my spending into one monthly report.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The aggregation of regional climate data allows researchers to identify broader patterns that individual observations may miss.

words.definitionEn: A state of worry or excitement that prevents calm behaviour.
words.exampleDailyEn: Her agitation grew as she searched for her missing keys.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Prolonged exposure to traffic noise may increase agitation and reduce residents' ability to concentrate at home.

words.definitionEn: Worry intensely while trying to make a difficult decision
words.exampleDailyEn: I agonized over which course to choose all weekend.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Many graduates agonize over whether to pursue further education or enter an increasingly competitive job market.

words.definitionEn: An illness, especially one that is not serious.
words.exampleDailyEn: The pharmacist suggested a remedy for my stomach ailment.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Treating minor ailments at local clinics can reduce pressure on hospitals and improve access to healthcare.

words.definitionEn: having no clear purpose, plan, or direction
words.exampleDailyEn: We spent the afternoon on an aimless walk.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Without clear learning goals, students may engage in aimless online browsing rather than developing useful research skills.

words.definitionEn: a passage through which air reaches the lungs
words.exampleDailyEn: The nurse checked that the patient's airway was clear.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Heavy traffic along a major airway requires careful coordination to keep aircraft safely separated.

words.definitionEn: Make someone feel unwelcome or unwilling to support you
words.exampleDailyEn: His constant complaints alienated even his closest friends.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public transport policies may alienate residents if local authorities fail to explain their benefits clearly.

words.definitionEn: The feeling of being disconnected from other people or society.
words.exampleDailyEn: Joining a local choir eased her sense of alienation.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Rapid urban development can deepen residents' alienation when familiar neighbourhoods are replaced by anonymous apartment blocks.

words.definitionEn: Burning or shining brightly.
words.exampleDailyEn: The candles were still alight when we arrived.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Passengers should wait until the bus has stopped completely before they alight from the vehicle.

words.definitionEn: The arrangement of objects in a straight line or correct position.
words.exampleDailyEn: The mechanic checked the alignment of my front wheels.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Closer alignment between school curricula and workplace needs could improve employment prospects for young graduates.

words.definitionEn: Loyalty and support given to a country, group, or leader.
words.exampleDailyEn: Despite moving abroad, he kept his allegiance to his hometown club.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Political allegiance can influence how voters interpret economic policies and assess the performance of elected officials.

words.definitionEn: to make pain, suffering, or a problem less severe
words.exampleDailyEn: A warm bath helped alleviate the ache in my shoulders.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Expanding affordable housing could alleviate pressure on low-income families and reduce the risk of homelessness.

words.definitionEn: A metal made by combining metals or adding other elements.
words.exampleDailyEn: This bicycle frame is made from a lightweight alloy.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Engineers are developing stronger alloys to reduce vehicle weight and improve fuel efficiency.

words.definitionEn: to refer to something without mentioning it directly
words.exampleDailyEn: He alluded to a surprise but gave no details.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The report alludes to funding difficulties without explaining how they might affect the proposed transport improvements.

words.definitionEn: relating to high mountains, especially the Alps
words.exampleDailyEn: Tiny alpine flowers grew between rocks beside the trail.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Rising temperatures threaten alpine ecosystems by reducing snow cover and forcing mountain species to move higher.

words.definitionEn: Having more than one possible meaning or interpretation
words.exampleDailyEn: His ambiguous reply left us unsure whether to come.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Ambiguous wording in public health advice can confuse readers and reduce their confidence in official guidance.

words.definitionEn: having conflicting feelings about someone or something
words.exampleDailyEn: I feel ambivalent about moving away from my family.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Many consumers remain ambivalent about online shopping because convenience must be balanced against concerns about privacy.

words.definitionEn: Something done to repair harm or show regret.
words.exampleDailyEn: I baked her a cake to make amends.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Companies should make amends for environmental damage by restoring habitats and compensating affected communities.

words.definitionEn: Friendly, pleasant, and easy to get along with.
words.exampleDailyEn: Our amiable neighbour always stops to chat by the gate.
words.exampleIeltsEn: An amiable manner can help healthcare professionals build trust with patients from diverse cultural backgrounds.

words.definitionEn: Surrounded by something, or during a particular situation
words.exampleDailyEn: We found a quiet bench amidst the flowering trees.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Amidst growing concerns about air quality, several cities have expanded their networks of protected cycle lanes.

words.definitionEn: A strong-smelling gas also dissolved in water for cleaning.
words.exampleDailyEn: This cleaning liquid contains ammonia, so keep the window open.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Ammonia emissions from agriculture can contribute to air pollution and damage sensitive natural habitats.

words.definitionEn: a unit used to measure electric current
words.exampleDailyEn: This small lamp draws less than one ampere.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Students measured the current in amperes to compare the electrical requirements of different household appliances.

words.definitionEn: an animal, such as a frog, living in water and on land
words.exampleDailyEn: We spotted a small amphibian beside the garden pond.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Declining amphibian populations may indicate changes in water quality and wider damage to freshwater ecosystems.

words.definitionEn: Enough or more than enough for a particular purpose
words.exampleDailyEn: We have ample time for breakfast before the train leaves.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Providing ample green space in residential areas can improve public health and encourage more active lifestyles.

words.definitionEn: the process of making a sound or signal stronger
words.exampleDailyEn: Without amplification, nobody could hear the singer outside.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The amplification of misleading claims through social media can undermine public trust in scientific research.

words.definitionEn: a device that increases the strength of sound or electrical signals
words.exampleDailyEn: He connected his guitar to a small amplifier.
words.exampleIeltsEn: An amplifier can make a speaker's voice clearly audible throughout a large lecture hall.

words.definitionEn: to make a sound or electrical signal stronger
words.exampleDailyEn: This small speaker amplifies music from my phone.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Social media can amplify public concerns about pollution, encouraging local authorities to respond more quickly.

words.definitionEn: To surgically remove all or part of a limb.
words.exampleDailyEn: The vet had to amputate the cat's badly injured leg.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Early treatment of severe infections can reduce the need to amputate limbs and improve patients' quality of life.

words.definitionEn: Similar in a way that allows a useful comparison.
words.exampleDailyEn: Our shared kitchen is analogous to a busy workshop.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The role of public libraries is analogous to that of schools in supporting lifelong learning within communities.

words.definitionEn: something similar to another thing in function or structure
words.exampleDailyEn: This wooden model is an analogue of the bridge.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Researchers use a mechanical analogue of the human heart to investigate how blood flows through damaged valves.
